title: Generic Structs
concept: Generic structs are types parameterized by other types — like Vec[T], Option[T], or your own Pair[T].
why: Most useful data structures are generic. A single Pair[T] definition works for Pair[Int], Pair[Str], Pair[Bool], and more.
tips: Generic structs are the backbone of reusable data structures
Use descriptive parameter names for multi-param types: Map[K, V], Entry[K, V], Result[T, E]
Methods on generic structs can introduce their OWN type parameters with separate names
Type constraints on the struct definition apply to ALL methods
common_mistakes: Forgetting to specify type parameters when constructing: `Pair{...}` instead of `Pair[Int]{...}`
Mixing up parameter order: Entry[K, V] vs Entry[V, K] — convention is key first
Putting constraints on the struct when they're only needed for specific methods
